sections.title: Welcome to Windmill Experience!
sections.preview: Get ready to step into the past! You won't need a time machine for this journey just some comfy shoes.

items.label: Travel Back in Time
items.text: Get ready to step into the past! You won't need a time machine for this journey just some comfy shoes.

items.label: A Restored Village
items.text: Thanks to the beautiful restoration by the Voudouris family, you will see exactly how islanders lived over a century ago, long before Wi-Fi was even invented. You'll also get to snoop around and uncover some secret history from the 1940s!

items.label: The Miller's Life
items.text: Today, you get to walk in the shoes of a real wind miller. Spoiler alert: his daily workout routine consisted of lifting heavy sacks of flour all day just to feed the majority of the village.

items.label: The Giant Windmill
items.text: Explore a real, working windmill from the bottom all the way to the top.

items.label: Village Life
items.text: Peek inside the traditional house and the bakery.

items.label: Nature & Animals
items.text: Sniff the wonderful herbs in our gardens, visit the threshing floor, and say hello to our lovely donkeys.

items.label: Underground Secrets
items.text: Walk straight through a real military tunnel!

details.text: How to Listen to the Tour

items.label: It's Super Easy

items.label: Listen Together
items.text: Choose your language, turn up your phone's volume or share headphones, and follow the numbers around the village.

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: Move forward to our gardens with herbs!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Secret Mission for Young Explorers!

items.label: Grab Your Artistic Equipment
items.text: We will give you a special Mylotopi Sketch and a few colored pencils to take with you.

items.label: Observe Everything
items.text: As you walk around today, keep your eyes wide open! Look very closely at the giant windmill, the heavy stones, and the old tools. Try to memorize all the beautiful colors you see.

items.label: Create a Masterpiece
items.text: When you finish your adventure and sit down to relax at our restaurant-café, you can color in your drawing and turn it into a true masterpiece!

sections.title: Our Garden with Our Herbs!
sections.preview: Take a deep breath! Does it smell like a giant outdoor kitchen or a village pharmacy? Actually, it’s both!

items.label: Kitchen or Pharmacy?
items.text: Take a deep breath! Does it smell like a giant outdoor kitchen or a village pharmacy? Actually, it’s both!

items.label: The Ultimate Survival Kit
items.text: Before modern medicine and supermarkets, these gardens were an island survival kit. These plots are filled with the exact same herbs that have grown here for centuries.

items.label: Nature's Doctor
items.text: Herbs like Thyme, Oregano, and Marjoram weren’t just used to make dinner taste amazing they were the local doctor! If someone had a stomach ache, the wind miller’s family wouldn't run to the pharmacy for bad-tasting pink syrup they would come right here to pick leaves for a natural remedy.

items.label: A Painter's Palette
items.text: Check out the beautiful purple Lavender and bright green Mint! They look like someone painted them right into the garden. Pay close attention to those bright colors!

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: Then move forward to the Historic Windmill!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Mission for our Young Plant Detectives and Adults!

items.label: Old-School Fun
items.text: Put the phones away for a second we are going completely old-school! Do you see the physical puzzle pieces scattered around?

items.label: Use Your Senses
items.text: Your job is to figure out which word belongs to which plant. You will have to use your eyes and your nose!

items.label: Rub and Sniff
items.text: Go ahead, give the leaves a tiny, gentle rub and a sniff (but please, no grazing don't eat the garden before lunch!).

items.label: Solve the Puzzle
items.text: Can you move the puzzle pieces to match the correct herbs? See if you can figure out the difference between the Mint and the Oregano. Which one smells like a delicious pizza, and which one smells like a cozy nap?

items.label: Sketchbook Reminder
items.text: Keep your eyes open, Plant Detectives! Remember the different colors of green, grey, and purple to color your Mylotopi Sketch later.

sections.title: The Windmill Base (1st Floor)
sections.preview: Welcome to the "Mill of the Priest"!

items.label: A Living Legend
items.text: Welcome to the "Mill of the Priest"! You are standing inside the oldest working windmill on the entire island and in the whole Dodecanese complex. It is over 400-years-old, operated daily all the way up until 1987, and is still a living machine that grinds flour today!

items.label: At the Entrance
items.text: As you step through the doorway, notice the traditional pomegranate hanging for good luck, alongside a small bottle of Holy Water from Mount Athos that is over 9-years-old.

items.label: Built for Storms
items.text: This giant machine is 6.2 meters tall, and the stone walls around you are 1.2 meters thick to keep the building safe from wild sea storms.

items.label: Massive Machinery
items.text: Up on the higher floors, there are two massive grinding stones that weigh one ton each that's over two tons together!

items.label: Ancient Wood
items.text: 80% of the wood in this building is original, and the rest was brought all the way from Mount Athos. Amazingly, some of the reused wooden parts spinning above are between 1,000 and 1,300-years-old!

items.label: To Your Right
items.text: See the area covered with a rag? That was the miller's storage room. Next to it, you will see a wooden donkey saddle and a threshing sledge that the miller's donkey would pull to separate the wheat. You can also spot everyday wooden tools and beautiful photos of other windmills across Greece.

items.label: The Fireplace
items.text: The miller didn't just use this for warmth! Look closely inside—do you see a can? That holds cow fat, which the miller melted to lubricate the moving parts of the windmill so they wouldn't squeak. Just above the fireplace is a photograph of Kostas Politis, the beloved owner of this windmill whose legacy lives on right here.

items.label: To Your Left
items.text: You will see a traditional scale and weights, which were used to carefully weigh the fresh flour.

items.label: The First Brakes
items.text: Look for the tiny rope hanging down. Believe it or not, that rope was the windmill's first braking system! The miller would pull it to lift those two-ton millstones just a tiny bit, making it safe for him to go outside and unwrap the sails.

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: Then move forward to the second floor of the Windmill!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A mission for our Young Explorers and Adults!

items.label: Test the Walls
items.text: Let's see just how thick those walls really are! Go stand next to the doorway and stretch your arms out as wide as you can. Are your arms longer than the wall is thick, or does the windmill win?

items.label: Spy
items.text: Look around the room and see if you can spot the wooden donkey’s saddle!

items.label: Find the Fat
items.text: Peer into the fireplace can you spot the hidden can of cow fat?

items.label: Spot the Brakes
items.text: Find the tiny hanging rope that acted as the windmill's braking system!

sections.title: The Windmill Sleeping Area (2nd Floor)
sections.preview: Welcome to the second floor! Watch your step on the wooden stairs and mind your head on the wood above. Get ready for a big surprise about how the family lived.

items.label: Watch Your Step
items.text: Welcome to the second floor! Watch your step on the wooden stairs and mind your head on the wood above. Get ready for a big surprise about how the family lived.

items.label: To Your Right
items.text: On the walls, you will see some beautiful pictures showing different historic windmills from all across Greece. But this space wasn't just a gallery!

items.label: A Very Noisy Bedroom
items.text: Right here on the right side is actually where the wind miller and his entire family used to sleep! Can you imagine trying to take a peaceful nap while the whole building was shaking, the wind was howling, and the heavy machinery was loudly crushing wheat just a few feet away? They must have been very heavy sleepers!

items.label: To Your Left
items.text: Now, look over to the left side. This was a very important and busy storage space.

items.label: Protecting the Flour
items.text: The miller used this side of the room to safely stack all the heavy bags of raw wheat waiting to be ground, alongside the freshly filled bags of fluffy white flour that were ready to go out and feed the village. He kept them right here near his bed so he could protect them!

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: Then move forward to the third floor of the Windmill!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Question for our Young Explorers and Adults!

items.label: Imagine This
items.text: Could you imagine yourself sleeping on the second floor exactly how they used to do?

sections.title: The Windmill Machinery (3rd Floor)
sections.preview: Welcome to the third floor! Please watch your step on the ladder and mind your head as you explore.

items.label: Mind Your Head
items.text: Welcome to the third floor! Please watch your step on the ladder and mind your head as you explore.

items.label: The Muscle of the Mill
items.text: You are now looking at the real power of the windmill. Look at that massive wooden beam above the stones. It is the main connector linking the heavy stones inside, the gears, and the giant spinning sails outside!

items.label: Two-Ton Stones
items.text: These massive grinding stones weigh over two tons together! They were imported all the way from Nisyros Island, which is famous for producing a unique, super-strong stone perfect for milling.

items.label: The Feeder & The Bell
items.text: Look just above the stones for a wooden box called The Feeder, where the miller poured the raw wheat. But how did he know when it was empty over all the loud noise? Look closely for a tiny bell! It would ring automatically when the wheat ran low to tell the miller to refill it.

items.label: The First Brake
items.text: See that wooden lever connected to a tiny rope? That connects all the way down to the first floor and is the first braking system we talked about downstairs.

items.label: Dropping the Flour
items.text: Look down near the lever to find a trap door connecting to a pipe. As soon as the flour was perfectly crushed, it dropped straight down that pipe to the bottom floor!

items.label: The Miller's "Tip"
items.text: Right next to the main pipe is a second, smaller trap door. In the old days, people didn't always pay with money. Instead, the miller used this door to collect his "tip" keeping a small percentage of the flour for his own family as payment for his hard work!

items.label: Smooth Spinning
items.text: Spot the little can near the trap doors. Downstairs he used cow fat, but up here, he used a special mixture of olive oil and soap to keep the upper gears running smoothly.

items.label: The Emergency Brake
items.text: Look next to the ladder for a really thick rope. If the miller needed to completely stop making flour in a hurry, he pulled this rope the second braking system!

items.label: A Ship's Ceiling
items.text: Lastly, look up at the ceiling. What does it remind you of? It is actually designed in the shape of a ship to enhance the power of the mechanism and produce flour more quickly!

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: Then move forward to the Threshing Floor and to the Donkeys Area!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Mission for our Young Explorers and Adults!

items.label: Listen for the Bell and Ring it
items.text: Can you find the tiny bell that warned the miller when the wheat was running out? Can you ring it?

items.label: Find the Hidden Flour
items.text: Scan the floor and see if you can spot the special "tip" door where the miller kept his hard-earned payment!

sections.title: Threshing Floor & the Donkeys!
sections.preview: Welcome back outside! Take a deep breath of fresh air. You are now standing near the traditional threshing floor, which looks a lot like a big, round stone dance floor.

items.label: Fresh Air & Stone Floors
items.text: Welcome back outside! Take a deep breath of fresh air. You are now standing near the traditional threshing floor, which looks a lot like a big, round stone dance floor.

items.label: The Dizzy Donkey
items.text: Look right in the middle of the circle at the wooden post. In the old days, the miller would loosely tie a rope from that post around a donkey's neck. The donkey's job was to walk round and round in a big circle, using its heavy feet to stomp and smash the harvested crops to break the seeds free!

items.label: Separating the Wheat
items.text: After the hardworking donkey did all of this dizzy stomping, the miller would step in to carefully separate the white wheat from the brown wheat. (Today, we don't use this method we buy our wheat directly from local producers on the island!)

items.label: Meet the Real Stars
items.text: You don't just have to imagine the animals! Look nearby and you will meet the real stars of the farm: our two lovely donkeys. The proud mama is named Melina, who is 6 years old, and her sweet little daughter is named Katie, who is just 2 years old.

items.label: The Missing Dad
items.text: As for Katie's dad... well, nobody actually knows where he went! He loved to sing really loud, so we think he walked to the next town to start a donkey rock band!

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: Then move forward to the Cellar/Italian Tunnel!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Mission for our Young Explorers and Adults!

items.label: The Donkey Dance
items.text: Step right up to the edge of the threshing floor! Can you pretend you are attached to the center wooden post and walk in a perfect circle just like a donkey did?

items.label: Say Hello
items.text: After your dizzy dance, make sure to go wave hello to Melina and Katie! Please admire our lovely donkeys from a distance! They look sweet, but they might mistake your fingers for baby carrots. We’d rather not find out!

sections.title: The Secret Tunnel & Cellar
sections.preview: Prepare yourselves for a total change of scenery as we head underground! As you step down into the cool air, take a look to your left and right.

items.label: A Change of Scenery
items.text: Prepare yourselves for a total change of scenery as we head underground! As you step down into the cool air, take a look to your left and right.

items.label: Decorative Bottles
items.text: You will see rows of local wine from the Skevofilax winery over in Kos. We keep these bottles here for design! Our actual drinking wines are kept safely in the main cellar, where the temperature is perfectly suited for them.

items.label: World War II History
items.text: Back in the 1940s, during World War II, this space wasn't for wine it was for survival. This 20-meter tunnel was built by Italian soldiers during the war.

items.label: The Hurry Tunnel
items.text: The soldiers used this passage as a hurry tunnel, a secret shortcut to run away and hide from their opponents. The cellar itself was used as a safe shelter where they could sleep, relax, and stay protected from the battles outside.

items.label: A Hidden Fortress
items.text: At the end of the tunnel, you will come out into our backyard, which is now our peaceful restaurant. But look back at the stone roof before you exit! In the 1940s, this entire area was a shooting range. The top was covered in heavy stone to protect the soldiers, and right at the edge, they had machine gun to defend the hillside. It’s hard to believe this quiet, beautiful spot for a meal was guarded place on the island!

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: When you finish exploring the tunnel, please come back and find our tour guide so they can show you the way to your next amazing stops the Traditional House and the Bakery!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Mission for our Young Explorers and Adults!

items.label: Top Secret
items.text: You are now on a secret mission! As you walk through the soldiers' tunnel, can you calculate exactly how many bottles of wine are lining the walls?

items.label: A Tiny, Crowded Home
items.text: Welcome to the traditional house! This amazing little home is over 130 years old. It measures less than 20 square meters, but believe it or not, 8 to 10 people used to live here! The grandparents, the parents, and all of their children shared this one single room.

items.label: Where Did Everyone Sleep?
items.text: The grandparents slept right over by the warm fireplace. The parents slept up high in the loft bed on the opposite side, while the older children slept in the beds next to it and on the couch.

items.label: Rock-a-Bye Baby
items.text: What about the baby? Look for the little wooden cradle! To help the baby fall asleep, someone could just gently pull that tiny hanging rope to rock it.

items.label: Clever Storage
items.text: Notice the space underneath the family beds that was their main storage room.

items.label: Daily Chores & Decor
items.text: Over on the left side, you can see a large wooden loom they used to make new clothes and repair old ones, alongside a chest where they kept their personal items. You’ll also spot a sifter used for flour, and beautiful old photographs and religious pictures on the walls.

items.label: Vases & Uniforms
items.text: Next to the chest, look for two vases: the large one was for wine, and the small one was for water. Just above them hang two beautiful traditional uniforms that the ladies of the house wore for weddings and special events.

items.label: The Heart of the Home
items.text: Since the house wasn't restored like modern homes, the fireplace was used to cook all their meals and keep the whole family warm. Right next to it is a small hand-grinder mill for grinding flour, along with their daily kitchenware and traditional plates decorated with pretty painted flowers.

items.label: The Hanging Swing
items.text: Look up at the ceiling! Do you see something hanging that looks a bit like a swing? It’s not for playing! They kept their fresh bread in the top part to keep it safely away from hungry mice. In the bottom part, they stored carobs. Back then, they didn't have candy bars, so sweet carobs were given to the children as a delicious chocolate treat!

items.label: A Traditional Refrigerator
items.text: Lastly, look for the wooden cabinet. Believe it or not, this is a traditional refrigerator! It has two parts. They put big ice cubes in the top, and as the ice melted, they could open a little tap to drink the ice-cold water. The cold from the top part also chilled the bottom section perfectly to keep their food fresh!

items.label: Upcoming
items.text: Then move forward to Bakery!

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Mission for our Young Explorers and Adults!

items.label: Spin the Mill
items.text: You have a lot to do in this busy little house! First, can you find the hand-grinder mill? Try putting the wooden handle into the gap and see if you can spin it around!

items.label: Look Up & Down
items.text: After your hard work, can you spot the hanging swing that kept the bread away from the mice?

items.label: Rock the Baby
items.text: What about the tiny rope they pulled to rock the baby to sleep? Can you make the baby fall asleep by rocking the rope? Is it hard for you?

items.label: Imagine This
items.text: Once you have found them all, imagine what it would be like sharing this small room with 8 to 10 of your family members!

items.label: A Community Hub
items.text: Welcome to the traditional oven! This beautiful stone oven is over 150 years old. Back in the day, the majority of the ladies in the village would come right here to bake their daily bread for their families.

items.label: A Two-Day Process
items.text: Baking bread back then wasn't as fast as just running to the supermarket! It was actually a two-day process. The night before, the ladies would carefully mix and shape the dough, leaving it to rest and rise up overnight.

items.label: Freshly Baked
items.text: The next morning, when the dough was ready, they would build a hot fire to warm up the oven. Once the temperature was just right, they placed the dough inside. After baking for one to two hours, the entire village would be filled with the delicious smell of fresh, warm bread ready to be eaten!

items.label: Historical Photos
items.text: If you look around, you can see some wonderful pictures on display that show exactly how they did this whole procedure.

challenge.label: For young visitors
challenge.title: A Question for our Young Explorers and Adults!

items.label: The Early Bird
items.text: The whole village needed fresh bread. Can you guess what time the baker had to wake up every morning to start making the dough? (Hint: It was long before the sun came up!)

items.label: Look Closely
items.text: Take a close look at the pictures to see how the village ladies used to work in the bakery.

items.label: Time to Relax
items.text: Now, it is time to head to the restaurant-café! Grab your colored pencils, enjoy a well-deserved snack, and finish making your Mylotopi Sketch a colorful masterpiece!

items.label: Thank You
items.text: Thank you for exploring with us today!
